result.title: Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression for Extreme Image Compression
result.summary: In the extreme-low bitrate range below $0.01$ bpp, image compression becomes a constrained generation problem: the reconstruction depends on inferring plausible missing details while staying close to the input image. Autoregressive token models provide an efficient coarse-to-fine prior for this setting, but the transmitted early-scale tokens often leave object identity and texture underdetermined, which can lead to source-inconsistent reconstructions. We introduce Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression (SAVAR), a generative codec built on Visual Autoregressive (VAR) modeling. SAVAR transmits early-scale tokens and a compact caption. The tokens provide image-specific layout information, while the caption supplies global semantics. SAVAR reconstructs a partial VQ-VAE latent from the retained scales, maps it to the start-of-sequence initialization, and uses the same latent to condition the caption embedding before adaptive layer normalization, separating two roles that are typically driven by a shared condition in VAR-style generation. On the Kodak and CLIC2020 datasets in the extreme-low range, SAVAR reduces perceptual distortion relative to matched ARPC retained-scale operating points, lowering LPIPS by about $8$--$9\%$ and DISTS by up to $22\%$ at a lower bpp. It reconstructs a $512 \times 512$ image in about $218$ ms on one NVIDIA L20X GPU, retaining fast autoregressive decoding in the evaluated setting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SAVAR，一个面向 0.01 bpp 以下极端低码率的生成式图像编解码器：基于 VAR 传输早期尺度 token 与紧凑 caption，用保留尺度重建的部分 VQ-VAE latent 同时初始化序列起始状态并条件化 caption 嵌入，从而在保持源一致性的同时快速重建。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不研究视觉推理，但其把同一 partial latent 拆成「序列起始初始化」与「条件注入」两种角色，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的初始化方式与视觉证据条件注入的分离设计提供可供核查的线索。
